The paper states that solar transits at different elevations "validated the assumption of separability" and concludes that "The validity of the separability assumption was subsequently verified by comparing data sets across different time intervals," but the actual evidence shown is only that several E-W transit cuts have similar widths; this does not by itself establish full 2-D separability across the whole beam or sidelobes.

The paper tests separability by verifying that the East-West "beam width remains largely invariant regardless of the Sun's position" across seven discrete solar zenith angles (Table 1 and Fig. 6), which validates the assumption for the main lobe along these specific tracks but does not rigorously demonstrate full two-dimensional separability.
